sections.h2: Where is Buchanan County, Iowa, and how is it organized?
sections.html:
Buchanan County is in northeast Iowa, and Independence is both the county seat and its largest city. Wikipedia reports that the county was formed on December 21, 1837, from part of Dubuque County and named for James Buchanan, then a senator and later the 15th president.

The county covers 573 square miles, nearly all of it land, and is divided into sixteen townships. It borders Clayton, Fayette, Delaware, Linn, Benton, Black Hawk and Bremer counties. The 2020 census counted 20,565 residents, down slightly from 20,958 in 2010, and about 67 percent of people live in rural areas. That rural share means a lot of Buchanan County sales involve acreage, outbuildings and well or septic questions rather than city lots.

Ten school districts reach into the county, including Independence, Jesup, Oelwein, Union, Vinton-Shellsburg and Wapsie Valley.

sections.h2: Which Buchanan County towns matter for a house sale?
sections.html:
Independence, Jesup and Fairbank are the three largest places, and each has a different feel. The 2020 census numbers below come from the county's Wikipedia page.

City2020 populationNote
Independence6,064County seat
Jesup2,508Partly in Black Hawk County
Fairbank1,111Partly in Fayette County
Winthrop823Smaller town
Hazleton713Near an Amish settlement
Quasqueton570Original county seat

Jesup's page says new subdivisions have followed its closeness to the Waterloo and Cedar Falls area, and its school district draws from both Buchanan and Black Hawk counties. A Jesup house that sits on the Black Hawk side of the line would be taxed by that county, so check which county the parcel is in. Hazleton has had an Old Order Amish settlement since 1914.

sections.h2: What is Independence, Iowa, known for?
sections.html:
Independence was founded June 15, 1847, and incorporated October 15, 1864. It took the county seat from Quasqueton, then a village of fewer than 15 residents. The county courthouse built in 1857 was replaced in 1939 by an Art Deco building.

In the late 1880s and early 1890s the town was a nationally known horse-racing center, nicknamed the "Lexington of the North." The Wapsipinicon River runs through the town, and a six-story grist mill built in 1867 still stands on the west bank. The state hospital on the west edge of town opened its main building in 1873.

Independence also has a small municipal airport and is served by the Independence Community School District, which also covers Brandon and Rowley. Cedar Rock, a state-owned Frank Lloyd Wright house, is about ten miles east near Quasqueton.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Buchanan County?
sections.html:
The county assessor values property, and the county treasurer bills and collects. Both offices are in the courthouse at 210 5th Avenue NE, Independence, IA 50644.

OfficeWhat it doesContact
TreasurerCollects tax, runs the tax sale, takes redemptions319-334-4340 (tax)
AssessorAssesses property, signs up homestead, veteran and family farm credits210 5th Ave NE

The treasurer's hours for property tax are Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the office closes at noon on June 30 and December 31, 2026, for balancing. Online payment is at pay.iowataxandtags.org by card or eCheck. The treasurer's county page is on Iowa Tax and Tags.

sections.h2: When are Buchanan County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Buchanan County taxes are due in two halves: the first on September 1 and the second on March 1. Each half is delinquent after the end of its month, September 30 and March 31. An owner can pay in full or in halves.

The state's calendar adds more detail. Annual statements are mailed in August. If a deadline lands on a weekend, it moves to the next business day. Unpaid first-half taxes become delinquent in October and unpaid second-half taxes in April, with interest of 1.5 percent per month, rounded to the nearest dollar, with a $1 minimum.

  • August: tax statements mailed.
  • September 1 to 30: first half payable without penalty.
  • March 1 to 31: second half payable without penalty.
  • Third Monday in June: annual county tax sale.

sections.h2: How do assessments and appeals work in Buchanan County?
sections.html:
Property owners can protest an assessment to the county board of review between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year. Iowa Code section 441.37 limits a protest to five grounds: the value is not equitable with like property, the property is assessed above the legal value, it is exempt or misclassified, there is an error, or there is fraud.

A written decision with reasons must come back from the board. If the board's answer does not satisfy you, an owner can go on to the Property Assessment Appeal Board or district court. Ask the Buchanan County Assessor which year the next reassessment falls in and whether informal reviews open earlier in April.

The county assessor's office also signs people up for the homestead, veteran and family farm credit programs, which can lower a bill before you ever need an appeal.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Buchanan County taxes?
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels are offered at the county tax sale, held each June by open bidding, and the third Monday in June is the standard date. A buyer pays the delinquent tax, and the owner who wants to redeem pays that amount plus 2 percent per month.

Redemption cannot be paid through the website. The treasurer asks owners to call 319-334-4340. If redemption is not completed in time, the buyer may start steps toward a tax deed, so a delinquent bill on a house you plan to sell is worth settling first. The county's office listing also mentions a cost of $4.00 per parcel on second-half delinquent taxes.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies when you sell in Buchanan County?
sections.html:
Iowa charges a real estate transfer tax of 80 cents for each $500 of value above $500, and the seller is liable for it. The tax is paid to the county recorder, and a declaration of value must be filed when the deed is presented, or the recorder will refuse to record it.

Iowa Code section 428A.2 lists exemptions, including gifts between spouses or between parent and child, transfers to heirs without consideration and tax deeds. A sale to a buyer at full price is taxable. Of each month's receipts, 82.75 percent go to the Department of Revenue and the rest stays in the county general fund.

sections.h2: What do Buchanan County sellers usually face?
sections.html: Sellers here often deal with older farmhouses, inherited homes and houses in towns with few buyers. A lender may ask for repairs that an owner cannot easily fund. In those cases a cash sale as-is can shorten the process, since we do not require inspections or repairs from the seller.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Buchanan County, Iowa?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Each half is delinquent after September 30 and March 31, and late interest is 1.5 percent per month.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Buchanan County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at the treasurer's office on the first floor of the courthouse, 210 5th Avenue NE, Independence, or online at pay.iowataxandtags.org. The tax phone is 319-334-4340.

faqs.q: When is the Buchanan County tax sale?
faqs.a: The annual sale is held in June, normally on the third Monday, though the treasurer may set another date.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Buchanan County assessment?
faqs.a: File a protest with the board of review between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year, on one of the grounds in Iowa Code section 441.37.

faqs.q: Does Iowa charge a transfer tax when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The rate is 80 cents per $500 of value above $500, the seller is liable, and the county recorder collects it with a declaration of value.
